Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 09:05:53 -0700
Subject: RE: production errors — immediate help needed

Summary of findings from bridge (09:00 PDT):
- Observed behavior: sudden drop in tokens/sec served from reserved pool RP-FTG-03 starting 07:48 PDT while incoming QPS remained ~steady. This produced queueing in the request router and backend 504 errors.
- Root cause hypothesis: runtime kernel selection regression triggered by a new quantized model variant in the control plane. The scheduler chose a conservative kernel path resulting in serialization of some ops at high concurrency.
- Evidence: kernel fallback logs + increased context-switch counters attached.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:10 PDT:
1) Forced routing to RP-FTG-03 fallback variant (non-quantized) to restore parallel execution.
2) Temporarily increased autoscale burst for RP-FTG-03 by +30% (30m window).
3) Enabled request-level prefix caching for high-volume routes to reduce token throughput.

Observed effect: tokens/sec recovered to ~92% of expected by 09:25 PDT; error rate dropped from 11% -> 1.8%. We’re keeping monitoring on.

Attachments: reserved_capacity_report.pdf (summary), kernel_fallback_snippet.txt (excerpt)

Marcus Lin
Staff SW Eng, Runtime | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 10:02:11 -0700
Subject: RE: production errors — immediate help needed

Claire / Oliver —

Short update: Marcus and the runtime team identified a kernel-selection regression tied to a model variant rollout. We applied three mitigations (fallback routing, temporary burst increase, prefix caching) and have brought throughput back to ~92% with error rate near baseline.

Next steps and asks:
- We will revert the problematic model variant in the control plane and schedule a safe re-roll after additional perf validation (ETA 48h).
- Redwood will run a post-incident perf regression check and provide a mitigation timeline + proposed credit.
- Can Fintegrate confirm tolerance for a short maintenance window (30–45m) to finalize reversion?

We understand the customer impact and will follow up with a detailed incident postmortem by EOD tomorrow.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll get you a formal remediation and a proposal for a stronger SLA guardrail.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- One-time credit to Fintegrate equivalent to 10% of June bill, applied as invoice credit.

We’ll set a working session with your platform team next week to review the postmortem and proposed SLA guardrails. Proposed times: Tue/Wed morning PDT.

Thank you for patience and for working the bridge with us.
